name: NTT DATA
summary: NTT DATA's careers FAQ describes a recruiter screen, a technical interview or assessment (a live technical discussion, a case-based conversation, a problem-solving exercise or a test on a third-party platform) and a hiring manager interview, usually between one and three interviews in all, with steps that vary by business unit, location and role. It publishes four values: Respect every voice, Think big. Be bold., Deliver the outcome, and Win together.
rounds: Online application, with an online aptitude or coding test for some graduate roles
Recruiter screen on your background, career goals and fit for the role
Technical interview or assessment: a live discussion, a case-based conversation or an online test
Hiring manager interview on communication, adaptability, collaboration and client work
For some roles, a further conversation on strategic thinking and values

questions.text: Tell me about yourself and what brings you to NTT DATA.
covers: Your background and the skills most relevant to this role
One achievement with a result
A specific reason for applying, in under two minutes

questions.text: Tell me about a time you changed your mind because of someone else's input.
covers: Your original view and whose input changed it
How you made room for their view, especially if they were junior or quiet
What the better decision led to

questions.text: Tell me about a time you proposed a bolder solution than the one people expected.
covers: The expected option and why it wasn't enough
Your proposal, and how you handled doubts and risks
What happened, including any part that didn't work

questions.text: Tell me about a time you delivered under pressure when the outcome mattered to a client or user.
covers: What was at stake for them and how tight the time was
What you prioritised and what you dropped
The outcome, ideally with a number

questions.text: Tell me about a win you shared with a team. What was your part?
covers: The goal and how the work was split
Your own contribution, in the first person
How the team celebrated or shared credit

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked with colleagues in another country or time zone.
covers: Who they were and what made working together hard
The habits you used: written handovers, overlap hours, clear owners
What it achieved and what you'd do differently

questions.text: Walk me through how you'd plan moving a client's on-premise application to the cloud.
covers: Assessing the application, its data and its dependencies first
Choosing an approach: move as it is, re-platform or rebuild parts
Testing, a cut-over plan with rollback, and cost and security checks

questions.text: A client reports that a nightly data load is missing records. What would you check first?
covers: Which records, since when, and whether the source sent them
The job's logs, filters, rejected rows and any schema change
Fixing and reloading safely, then telling the client what happened

questions.text: Explain microservices versus a monolith, and when you'd keep the monolith.
covers: A monolith is one deployable application; microservices split it into small services
Microservices help teams scale and release separately but add network and operations complexity
Keeping a monolith for a small team or a simple, stable product

questions.text: A client wants to cut support tickets by a third. How would you work out where they come from and what to fix?
covers: Grouping tickets by type, product, channel and customer
Finding the few causes behind most tickets
Fixes such as product changes, self-service help or automation, and how you'd track the drop

questions.text: How would you explain a serious technical risk to a client executive in two minutes?
covers: The risk in business terms: what could happen and how likely
The options, with cost and time for each
Your recommendation and the decision you need from them

questions.text: For experienced candidates: describe an engagement where the client's priorities changed. How did you adjust the plan?
covers: What changed and why
How you re-planned scope, people and dates with the client
The result and the relationship afterwards

questions.text: Why NTT DATA, and what do you know about the industries it serves?
covers: Something specific: a service line, an industry or recent work you read about
How your skills fit it
What you hope to learn there

questions.text: What would you want to achieve in your first six months here?
covers: Learning the team, the client and the systems quickly
One or two concrete contributions you'd aim for
A question back about how success is judged in the role

tips: NTT DATA's FAQ says the technical stage can be a live discussion, a case, a problem-solving exercise or an online test; ask your recruiter which to expect.
Prepare client stories: the hiring manager interview looks at client engagement, communication and adaptability.
Have a short example ready for each of the four values, especially delivering an outcome and winning as a team.
Steps vary by business unit, location and role, so read the job post closely and plan for each stage it names.
